rows.bmrInterpretation: Adequate BMR. Helps maintain a healthy calorie deficit without slowing your metabolism.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Healthy Fat Range. Safe to cut calories without losing muscle.

rows.bmrInterpretation: Mildly suppressed BMR. Monitor how your metabolism responds over time.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Above Healthy Range. Higher risk for heart and metabolic issues; losing weight is recommended.

rows.bmrInterpretation: Suppressed BMR. The body may start breaking down muscle for energy; recovery nutrition is recommended.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Obese Range. Professional guidance for weight loss is recommended.

rows.bmrInterpretation: Severely suppressed BMR. The body may be conserving energy excessively; medical guidance is recommended.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Severely Obese. See a doctor before trying any diet on your own.
rows.scientificNotes: Fat <15% risks fat-soluble vitamin deficiency (WHO min)

rows.bmrInterpretation: BMR supports muscle growth. Your body has enough energy to build muscle.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Lean-to-moderate BF%. Your hormone levels are in a great spot to build muscle effectively.

rows.bmrInterpretation: Marginal BMR. Your energy levels may slightly limit muscle growth.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Slightly elevated BF%. Muscle gain is possible but will be slower; focus on losing some fat while building muscle at the same time.
rows.scientificNotes: Protein below optimal for muscle protein synthesis

rows.bmrInterpretation: Low BMR. Your body may lose muscle faster than it builds it.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: High BF%. Your body isn't in the right state to bulk up; lose fat first before trying to build muscle.
rows.scientificNotes: Fat floor raised to 15% per WHO minimum; protein critically low

rows.bmrInterpretation: Severely low BMR. Your body may not have enough energy to build muscle properly.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Very high BF%. Excess body fat is causing inflammation that blocks muscle building; medical advice needed before starting any program.
rows.scientificNotes: Fat <10% is physiologically unsafe; corrected to <15%

rows.bmrInterpretation: Normal BMR. Supports stable energy levels throughout the day.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Healthy composition. Your body stores and burns energy efficiently.
rows.scientificNotes: Protein ceiling raised to 28% to prevent muscle catabolism

rows.bmrInterpretation: Mild metabolic slowdown. Low energy levels may occur during the day.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Excess fat slightly impairs mitochondrial efficiency. Extra fat is making your cells less efficient at producing energy, so you'll feel tired more easily.

rows.bmrInterpretation: Low BMR. May be linked to hormone imbalance and ongoing tiredness.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Adiposity-linked fatigue. Excess fat is causing inflammation that drains your energy at a cellular level.

rows.bmrInterpretation: Severely low BMR. Persistent fatigue may occur; medical evaluation is recommended.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Severe obesity-related metabolic depression. Your body's energy systems are significantly affected; a full medical check-up is essential.

rows.bmrInterpretation: Healthy BMR. Supports balanced metabolism and stable energy regulation.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Visceral fat low. Your internal fat levels are healthy, your body handles sugar well, and your cholesterol levels are likely in good shape.
rows.scientificNotes: Fats must be predominantly unsaturated (MUFA+PUFA >2/3 of fat intake)

rows.bmrInterpretation: Early signs of metabolic slowdown; check fasting glucose and HbA1caEarly metabolic slowdown. Monitor blood sugar and metabolism regularly.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Rising visceral fat likely. Fat is starting to build up around your organs, and your body may be losing its ability to manage blood sugar; time to make lifestyle changes.

rows.bmrInterpretation: Impaired Metabolism. Blood sugar imbalance may be developing; medical screening is advised.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Visceral adiposity probable. Fat around your organs is likely causing broader health risks; blood sugar and cholesterol tests are needed.

rows.bmrInterpretation: Severely low BMR. May indicate a serious metabolic issue; medical attention is recommended.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Clinically obese. High risk of diabetes, cholesterol problems, and fatty liver disease; medical attention needed right away.

rows.bmrInterpretation: BMR supports aerobic capacity. Your body burns fat well during moderate exercise.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Lean BF% optimal for VO2max and running economy. Your body fat is at the perfect level for endurance; your body is built to go the distance.

rows.bmrInterpretation: Moderate BMR. Some fitness is there, but your body takes longer to bounce back after workouts.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Slightly excess BF% reduces power-to-weight ratio. The extra fat is making you carry more weight than needed, which slows you down and reduces stamina.

rows.bmrInterpretation: Below-par BMR. You'll tire out quickly and risk burning your body out from too much training.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Elevated BF% significantly burdens cardiovascular system. Higher body fat means your heart has to work much harder during long or intense exercise.
rows.scientificNotes: Fat floor raised from 10-14% to 15-19% per WHO minimum

rows.bmrInterpretation: Very low BMR. Your body isn't in a state where cardio/endurance workouts will help- you may actually get worse, and risk under-fuelling your body.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Very high BF% severely limits endurance. Excess fat puts serious strain on your joints and heart, making sustained exercise very difficult.
rows.scientificNotes: Fat <10% is physiologically unsafe; corrected to <15%

rows.bmrInterpretation: Elevated RMR reflects good muscle mass. Good amount of muscle, and your body is in a great state to build even more.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Lean BF% favours neuromuscular efficiency and power output. Your body fat is at an ideal level where your muscles and nerves work together efficiently for maximum strength.

rows.bmrInterpretation: Adequate but not ideal RMR. You can still build strength, but you'll need a solid, consistent workout plan to see results.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Moderate BF%; strength gains possible but hormonal environment less favourable. You can still build strength, but your hormone levels aren't quite optimal to support it fully.
rows.scientificNotes: Protein below optimal for strength adaptation

rows.bmrInterpretation: Low RMR suggests insufficient muscle mass baseline. Not enough muscle to start with, so focus on building muscle before anything else.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Higher BF% blunts testosterone response to training. Excess fat reduces your body's hormonal response to workouts; focus on losing fat and recomposing your body first.
rows.scientificNotes: Fat floor raised to 15% per WHO minimum

rows.bmrInterpretation: Very low RMR; insufficient muscle substrate. Your body doesn't have enough muscle to make strength training worthwhile right now.
rows.bodyFatInterpretation: Very high BF% creates systemic inflammation; injury risk elevated. Excess fat is causing widespread inflammation in your body, raising your injury risk; get medical clearance before training.
rows.scientificNotes: Fat <10% is physiologically unsafe; corrected to <15%
